Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To get our dedicated sizing pass in front of engineering this week I put together a short, SLA-focused questionnaire that helps us size two things simultaneously: the baseline reserved pool for sustained traffic and a burst-capacity plan (how much transient GPU headroom you want + fallback behavior).

A couple of notes up front: our sizing will assume the model variant you indicated (redwood-gpt-13b-q4f16) unless you request a different quantization/variant. If you have a second variant for lower-cost fallback, please note it. Also, if strict tenant isolation (no oversubscribe on the same GPU) is required, call that out — it materially increases commit.

Quick ask: can you fill the table at the bottom and return by EOD tomorrow? We can turn these answers into a quick fleet sketch (GPU count, on-demand burst, warm pool sizing) and a recommended canary seeding plan.

Questions (short answers are fine):
1) Traffic shape: typical RPS during business hours (Mon-Fri 9-18 in PST) and peak RPS observed in the last 30 days.
2) Request mix: percent interactive chat vs. batch/generation vs. embedding/rerank.
3) Prompt length distribution (tokens): median, 75th, 95th for prompt only.
4) Output length distribution (tokens): median, 75th, 95th.
5) Session affinity: average session duration and average requests per session (if you maintain sessions/KV cache).
6) KV cache hit expectation (if you use session caching): estimate or range (0-100%).
7) p50/p95/p99 latency targets (in ms) for interactive requests.
8) Tolerance for preemption/on-demand fallback (can you accept increased latency for 10-30s window during overflow?)
9) Canary plan: percent of traffic to seed a new model/size when we rollout (if you have a preference).
10) Any regulatory/airgap requirements or strict retention rules that affect our ability to route to multi-tenant hosts?

Attachment: I included a stub CSV template (stormlabs_token_profile.csv) for token histograms if you have telemetry.

Thanks — Camila

Camila —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers below (we'll attach a CSV tomorrow with histograms). High level: we care most about p95 for UX; p99 can be relaxed to allow fallback to a cheaper variant. We can tolerate short fallback windows but prefer graceful degradation (e.g., degrade to 2s p95 rather than error).

1) Traffic shape: baseline 35 RPS, business peak ~110 RPS (we saw spikes to 200 RPS during feature launches).
2) Request mix: 70% interactive chat, 20% embedding/rerank, 10% batch (async long jobs).
3) Prompt tokens: median 42, 75th 110, 95th 320.
4) Output tokens: median 48, 75th 160, 95th 420.
5) Session affinity: sessions ~4 minutes avg, ~6 requests per session. We use KV cache aggressively for conversation continuity.
6) KV cache hits: ~62% for conversational flows, near 80% for some chat-heavy endpoints.
7) Latency targets: p50 60ms, p95 450ms, p99 target 1500ms (we accept relaxed p99 when falling back).
8) Preemption tolerance: yes, we can tolerate 20-30s degraded windows; prefer queued slow-path rather than hard errors.
9) Canary: start at 5% then 25% then 100% over 48h if no regressions.
10) Compliance: no airgap; data residency US only. No additional retention constraints beyond our standard logs (30d).

We'll upload the token-level CSV tomorrow evening.

—Ethan

On a separate note: what would a 99th percentile warmpool look like for our workload? Curious how that maps to GPU count for the redwood-gpt-13b-q4f16 variant.

Forwarding Ethan's answers from StormLabs. Key takeaways for sizing:
- Baseline steady 35 RPS with frequent burst events up to 200 RPS.
- Heavy conversational workload with solid KV cache (60-80% hit).
- Prompt/output tails are long (95th tokens 320/420) which increases per-request GPU time.
- Latency objective is p95 ~450ms; p99 can be relaxed to 1.5s with fallback.

Action items: can we produce a quick two-scenario sketch?
A) conservative reserved commit (no GPU oversubscribe) sized for steady 35 RPS + 1.5x buffer for mid-week churn, plus warm pool to carry 99th percentile baseline. B) cost-aware plan: modest reserved commit (cover 70% baseline), with on-demand burst and fallback mixing to a smaller quantized variant for tail events.

Please estimate: GPU type(s) (A100xTB/RTX8000 mix), count for reserved pool, warm pool size (standby VMs with warmed KV caches), expected p95 under both plans, and rough monthly cost delta. Attach one-pager to return to Ethan and recommend canary seed sizes.

Thanks — Camila

Camila / team —

Quick sizing sketch attached (sla-burst-probing-checklist.pdf) and rough numbers inline:
- Assumptions: redwood-gpt-13b-q4f16 throughput = ~11 tokens/ms on A100-80GB for typical sequence lengths; smaller fallback variant (redwood-gpt-13b-q4f8) gives ~1.8x throughput improvement. KV cache effective token reduction = 60% overall (we used Ethan's 62% as baseline).

Plan A (conservative, no oversubscribe):
- Reserved: cover 35 RPS steady + 50% buffer => 52.5 RPS sustained. Considering avg request token work = prompt+output ~90 tokens median but 95th tails push average to ~180 tokens across distribution -> conservative avg token-per-request estimate = 150 tokens. => sustained token/sec = 52.5 * 150 = 7,875 tokens/sec.
- A100 effective tokens/sec per GPU (with KV savings) ~ 11k tokens/sec => GPUs reserved = ceil(7875/11000) = 1 (we still recommend 2 for redundancy and rolling maintenance).
- Warm pool (to hit 99th baseline spikes): target to absorb spikes to 200 RPS for short windows. To cover 200 RPS with same avg token/request 150 -> 30k tokens/sec. Burst headroom GPUs = ceil(30000/11000) = 3 GPUs. So recommended cluster = 2 reserved + 3 warm (hot-standby) => 5 total with warm autoscale.
- Expected p95: ~350-450ms under reserved; ~600-900ms when warm pool spins up if using on-demand nodes.

Plan B (cost-aware hybrid):
- Reserved: cover 70% baseline (24.5 RPS) => sustained tokens/sec ~3675 -> GPUs reserved = 1 (but again 2 recommended for HA).
- On-demand burst: allow autoscale + fallback to q4f8 variant for overflow. Fallback reduces token work per GPU by ~1.8x so burst GPUs required smaller. To handle 200 RPS with fallback mixing -> 2-3 on-demand GPUs + 1 warm standby.
- Expected p95: ~300ms for reserved traffic; tail p95 ~1.2-2.0s during large spikes depending on fallback split.

Estimated monthly delta (very rough): Plan A ~ $85k/mo (reserved + warm pool baseline), Plan B ~ $48k/mo (smaller commit + burst ops). Real costs depend on committed discounts and cloud region.

Next steps: I can turn this into a one-pager with a cost table and rollout/canary steps for Ethan. Laura — can you validate the latency numbers with runtime team? Marissa — can you draft the canary traffic cadence for the 5/25/100% progression?
